relevance_note: Case report of a Japanese girl with infantile-onset IBD in whom WES and SNP array found 'a novel de novo 119 kb microdeletion containing only TNFAIP3', plus a literature table (Table 1) of four previously published HA20 patients with TNFAIP3 deletions.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in my scratch directory assembled the JSON and checked every span verbatim. Table 1 has patients as columns; its column header row is the 'References' row ('This report', '(Shimizu et al.^10)', '(Tsuchida et al.^8)', '(Tsuchida et al.^8)', '(Franco-Jarava et al.^9)'). Columns are numbered 1-5 left to right; column 1 ('This report') is the first-hand proband ('patient'). Columns 2-5 are previously published patients with no patient label in the paper, so they are labelled 'Table 1 column N (reference)'. The script cut the Table 1 spans and cell values from the table lines, and I checked them against the table. CONTRADICTIONS/INCONSISTENCIES: (1) Allele labelling at c.305A>G (NM_001270507.2). HGVS 'c.305A > G' implies A is the reference allele, but the text calls the father's G/G 'homozygous for the reference allele' and says the patient was 'homozygous (A/A)' for this variant and that it was 'also observed in the heterozygous state (A/G) in her mother'. Recorded as stated: patient homozygous, mother heterozygous, and no variant row for the father. The authors read the apparent homozygosity as a sign of the deletion and call the variant 'relatively common (MAF = 0.0117)'. They do not classify it, so pathogenicity is not reported. (2) Deletion size: CNV analysis of the WES data (EXCAVATOR2) gave 'a single de novo 187 kb microdeletion within the TNFAIP3 gene', while the SNP array 'validated' '119 kb microdeletion involving only TNFAIP3'. The 119 kb arr[GRCh37] string is recorded. OTHER NOTES: Zygosity 'heterozygous' for the deletion comes from 'HA20 caused by TNFAIP3 heterozygous microdeletion' (said of the present case) and 'lost the paternal allele'. 'de novo' is stated by the authors; the SNP array covered only the patient and her father; the mother's deletion status is covered only by the family WES/CNV 'de novo' call. Grandparents: DNA was extracted and they appear in the Fig. 1D pedigree, but the text gives no number, labels or genotypes, so they have no rows. The proband was '8-month-old' at presentation and Table 1 gives age at diagnosis 8 months. Follow-up continued (setons for 1 year) without a stated age, so age at last evaluation is not reported. 'afebrile' at the 8-month evaluation is a point-in-time statement, not a contradiction of the intermittent fever; the recurrent fever checklist item stays observed. Not recorded: screening tests at 1 month 'not consistent with primary immunodeficiency, autoinflammatory disease, or hemophagocytic syndrome' (diagnostic exclusions, not features); 'no ... other significant family medical history' (no specific feature, so the parents' checklist items are not reported); negative IL10/IL10R results; a database accession printed for the deletion (no field). Checklist judgements (kept conservative): perianal or anal ulcers and 'gastroenteritis' were not counted as 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' (columns 2 and 5 not reported). 'thyroiditis' (column 4) is not stated to be autoimmune, so autoimmune thyroiditis is not reported. Headache and psychomotor delay were not counted as CNS involvement. Hepatosplenomegaly and enlarged tonsil were not counted as lymphoproliferation. 'abnormal condition of the autoimmune system' (Supplementary Table S1, not available) was not counted as autoantibodies. Column 5 'Upper respiratory infections' (plural) was counted as recurrent infections, 'Neutrophilic dermatosis' as a skin lesion, and 'growth ... delay' as growth failure. Column 2 (Shimizu): range printed as '—', involved region 'TNFAIP3 (exons 2−3)'; the variant string is taken from the text sentence, and cytoband 6q23.3 is recorded as the coordinates. 'variant_type = large deletion/CNV' is used for all deletions, including the 5 kb one. n_patients_reported = 1 (the first-hand case); cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is left null because the proband is not said to be previously reported, and the Table 1 patients carry source_reference_in_review. The two Tsuchida patients are kept separate; their relationship is not stated. The proband's colchicine and 5-aminosalicylic acid appear only in Table 1. '...' in feature_text marks words omitted from a table cell.
